{"id": "31:14/q14", "question": "Does 'in two years' require nursing for the whole period?", "turns_on": "Whether fī names the full endpoint alone or allows a weaning event within the two-year interval.", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q14/p1", "position": "The expression describes weaning at the completion of two full years, the complete nursing term.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī, al-Ṭabrisī and Ibn Kathīr compare 2:233; al-Ṭabrisī explicitly says two full years. Ibn al-Jawzī, al-Bayḍāwī, al-Nasafī and Bursevī say the endpoint is two years. Al-Damghānī compares 2:233's two complete ḥawls and 2:240's ḥawl as a year. Al-Biqāʿī notes hardship through those years; Study Quran says full breastfeeding is best when possible, comparing 2:233 and 46:15."}, {"id": "31:14/q14/p2", "position": "Two years is the normal or maximum period; parents may wean earlier when the child’s welfare warrants it.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī draws this from the preposition fī; Kuran Yolu compares 2:233. Asad says the literal phrase describes weaning within two years. This position need not deny that two years completes the term. Al-Kashshāf leaves earlier weaning to the mother's judgment of whether the child is strong enough, comparing 2:233."}, {"id": "31:14/q14/p3", "position": "Weaning is after two years; fī can mean 'after' in this phrase.", "reasons": "Al-Burhān expressly reads fī as baʿda, 'after,' here."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q15", "question": "How is 'his weaning is in two years' parsed?", "turns_on": "Whether to supply an implied word of completion or state the surface subject-predicate relation.", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q15/p1", "position": "An implied 'completion' means his weaning is at the completion of two years.", "reasons": "Al-Akhfash supplies the omitted completion; al-Wāḥidī explains the completed two-year sense."}, {"id": "31:14/q15/p2", "position": "The noun is subject and the prepositional phrase is predicate.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī gives this construction and says it foregrounds two years of maternal nursing hardship."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q16", "question": "Why use ʿāmayn for the two years?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q16/p1", "position": "ʿĀm can evoke ease or joy, unlike sana for hardship, reflecting parental joy even in demanding infant care.", "reasons": "Bursevī contrasts عام with سنة, the latter often used for hardship or drought; al-Biqāʿī says the parents rejoice in caring for the child despite the hard two years. Al-Damghānī relates the term to ḥawl as a year in 2:233 and 2:240."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q17", "question": "What does the two-year term govern for nursing duties and maintenance?", "turns_on": "The notes distinguish the agreed maintenance period from stages of obligation, recommendation and permission.", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q17/p1", "position": "Two years is the agreed nursing or maintenance period, and the father’s nursing wage ends then.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Qurṭubī and Abū Ḥayyān state agreement on the period for maintenance or rulings while separating milk kinship. Bursevī says by agreement the father's nursing wage ceases after two years."}, {"id": "31:14/q17/p2", "position": "Nursing is obligatory until the child is self-sufficient, recommended through two years, and permissible through two and a half.", "reasons": "Bursevī reports this framework with al-Shāfiʿī and says the remaining dispute is about the effect on milk kinship."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q18", "question": "When does nursing establish milk kinship or its prohibition?", "turns_on": "Whether the verse fixes two years as a hard legal limit, permits adjacent days or six months, or whether actual weaning or age rather than the verse's term controls.", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q18/p1", "position": "Only nursing within two years establishes milk kinship; even a moment afterward does not.", "reasons": "Al-Shāfiʿī uses the two-year limit and a Prophetic report; Yaḥyā cites a report that there is no nursing after weaning and that Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās did not count nursing after two years. Al-Ālūsī lists al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Abū Yūsuf, Muḥammad, al-Ṭaḥāwī and a report from Mālik. Elmalılı says the fatwa follows the two Imams and prefers it over Abū Ḥanīfa's precaution."}, {"id": "31:14/q18/p2", "position": "Nursing for a few contiguous days or up to an adjacent month after two years still establishes milk kinship.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī attributes a few extra days to Mālik; Ibn ʿAṭiyya notes connected days; al-Qurṭubī mentions one adjacent month if nursing continues. The reports vary in precise extension."}, {"id": "31:14/q18/p3", "position": "The prohibition extends six months beyond two years, for thirty months total.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥanīfa relates the thirty months of pregnancy and weaning in 46:15 to each named period; al-Ālūsī gives his analogy of two debts due in a year or two obligations from one debtor. Elmalılı calls it precaution and says the fatwa instead follows the two Imams. Al-Burhān reports Abū Ḥanīfa's reasoning that the full thirty-month term can apply to each named matter, with the additional six months assigned to nursing because pregnancy is shorter and children move to other food."}, {"id": "31:14/q18/p4", "position": "The prohibition has no fixed age limit and applies to adults as to children.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī reports this from some Medinans."}, {"id": "31:14/q18/p5", "position": "Only nursing in the first year establishes milk kinship.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī lists this among differing juristic opinions."}, {"id": "31:14/q18/p6", "position": "Early weaning can end the effect of later milk, even before the two years expire.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Qurṭubī record disagreement on whether milk after early weaning still creates the prohibition. Al-Kashshāf attributes to Abū Ḥanīfa a distinction after early weaning: later milk is ineffective if the child is self-sufficient on food, but establishes kinship if the child still needs milk."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q19", "question": "What minimum pregnancy duration follows from the two-year nursing term?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q19/p1", "position": "Six months is the minimum: thirty months for pregnancy and weaning in 46:15 minus the full twenty-four months of nursing.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās and other imams make the inference in Ibn Kathīr, comparing 46:15 with 2:233; Ṭabāṭabāʾī and Samarrāʾī state the same deduction, the latter attributing it to some jurists. Al-Burhān attributes this calculation to ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās and says al-Shāfiʿī adopts it."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q20", "question": "What maximum gestation does ʿĀʾisha's report give in this discussion?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q20/p1", "position": "A child is never in the womb longer than two years, even by a spindle coil’s time.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports ʿĀʾisha's statement as treated as transmitted from the Prophet; it shortens the gestation allocation while preserving an explicit nursing term, although al-Ālūsī says the argument needs discussion."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q21", "question": "How does an ishkur relate grammatically to waṣṣaynā?", "turns_on": "Whether an explains the preceding command, supplies its governed verbal noun, or expresses its purpose or apposition.", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q21/p1", "position": "An is explanatory: the command means 'We said, give thanks.'", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Wāḥidī's author of al-Naẓm, al-Nasafī, Elmalılı and Ṭabāṭabāʾī explain the charge this way. Al-Naḥḥās prefers this against the infinitival analysis; Abū Ḥayyān records that preference. Al-Ālūsī says the imperative does not bar this parse."}, {"id": "31:14/q21/p2", "position": "An introduces an accusative verbal-noun complement governed by waṣṣaynā: God enjoined giving thanks.", "reasons": "Al-Zajjāj and Ibn al-Jawzī give the accusative parse; al-Samīn and al-Qurṭubī report it. Al-Ālūsī says an imperative does not invalidate the analysis."}, {"id": "31:14/q21/p3", "position": "It expresses the command's purpose, or is an apposition to parents: care for them by gratitude.", "reasons": "Al-Bayḍāwī allows explanation, motivation or apposition; Bursevī allows purpose. Al-Ālūsī reconstructs li-taʿlīl or an apposition, calls the last remote, and answers the objection based on the imperative."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q22", "question": "What form does commanded gratitude to God and parents take?", "turns_on": "Whether to state the general obligation and its grounds or a concrete devotional expression; al-Ālūsī treats the latter as an example.", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q22/p1", "position": "Thank God for creation, faith and His blessings through praise and obedience; thank parents for birth, raising and care through kindness, obedience, service, ties and prayer.", "reasons": "Muqātil and al-Wāḥidī name Islam or faith and parents' benefits; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses gratitude as obedience. Al-Ṭabarī adds care until the child's strength matures. Al-Māwardī, al-Ṭabrisī and Study Quran contrast praise and obedience with kindness and kinship. Bursevī adds reverence toward God and compassion toward parents; Elmalılı adds service and prayer, referring to al-Isrāʾ. Al-Ālūsī records prayer and fasting toward God and kinship toward parents; al-Ālūsī says the five-prayer example is illustrative rather than exhaustive. Al-Qushayrī argues from the agreed need for sustained obedience to parents that thanks to God requires using blessings in obedience rather than sin; he names glorification for God and provision for parents. Iṣlāḥī distinguishes parental gratitude and service from worship and says true thanks fulfills promises, not merely verbal thanks."}, {"id": "31:14/q22/p2", "position": "Performing the five daily prayers thanks God, and supplicating for one's parents after them thanks the parents.", "reasons": "Sufyān b. ʿUyayna's explanation is repeated by al-Baghawī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Qurṭubī, al-Nasafī, Bursevī and al-Ālūsī; al-Ālūsī says it illustrates some forms

{"id": "31:14/q23", "question": "Why is thanks to parents paired with thanks to God, and why is God named first?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q23/p1", "position": "God is the ultimate creator and giver; parents are appointed, proximate causes of birth and care, so gratitude to them follows gratitude to Him.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭāʾ distinguishes ultimate Cause and means, noting that absorption in one can eclipse the other. Al-Māwardī says Qatāda distinguishes God's right from theirs. Al-Ṭabrisī, al-Biqāʿī, Bursevī, Asad and Kuran Yolu emphasize source versus parental means; Bursevī cites Sharḥ al-Ḥikam and the hadith 'who does not thank people does not thank God,' giving two readings: a condition of valid thanks, or God's reward limited to those who thank His servants. Al-Ālūsī says their gratitude depends on His and that this explains divine priority. Asad compares 17:23–24. Iṣlāḥī says parents have the greatest right after God because they bring a person into existence and nourish them."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q24", "question": "What does the lām in ushkur lī do?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q24/p1", "position": "It strengthens the verb 'give thanks' and is conventionally attached to shukr.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr compares the usage at 2:152; he adds that the present tense of yashkur in the related passage signals renewed gratitude."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q25", "question": "What does 'to Me is the return' mean?", "turns_on": "Whether the clause is explained through resurrection and accounting or through God's sole sovereignty at the final state.", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q25/p1", "position": "All return to God at resurrection for judgment and recompense for gratitude, ingratitude and deeds, with Paradise or Fire as the outcome.", "reasons": "Yaḥyā names Resurrection; al-Ṭabarī says judgment on thanks and filial kindness. Al-Māwardī specifies Paradise and Fire; Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil through al-Wāḥidī say each is repaid for deeds. Muʿādh's prophetic mission report in Ibn Kathīr identifies everlasting Paradise or Hell. Bursevī, al-Ālūsī and Elmalılı stress reward or questioning."}, {"id": "31:14/q25/p2", "position": "Returning to God is reaching the state where no judge or owner exists but Him.", "reasons": "Bursevī gives this further explanation of the return."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q26", "question": "What role does the final return clause play in the parental counsel?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q26/p1", "position": "It warns and gives the reason to obey the command, since God will reckon gratitude and disobedience.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū Ḥayyān call it an inserted warning; al-Ṭabrisī calls it a threat. Bursevī and al-Ālūsī say return explains why obedience is required. Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the shift of person accords with 31:12."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q27", "question": "What reports link parental pleasure or neglect with the final reward?", "turns_on": "The cited reports give distinct formulations of the reward and consequence of filial conduct.", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q27/p1", "position": "God's pleasure follows a parent's pleasure, and His anger follows a parent's anger; pleasing or angering parents bears on Paradise or Hell.", "reasons": "Yaḥyā reports the correspondence and gate imagery even when a child was wronged; al-Māwardī transmits the Prophetic saying through ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar."}, {"id": "31:14/q27/p2", "position": "A servant who fulfills other obligations but neglects filial piety will not enter Paradise.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī quotes al-Firdaws via Abū al-Dardāʾ, without grading, and connects filial honor to monotheism, prayer and remembrance."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q28", "question": "How can one honor parents after their death?", "turns_on": "The reports prescribe different posthumous acts, one general and one fixed devotional sequence.", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q28/p1", "position": "Keep ties with a deceased father's friends; prayer and charity for deceased parents can restore dutifulness after earlier neglect.", "reasons": "Bursevī transmits these practices as reports."}, {"id": "31:14/q28/p2", "position": "A specified Thursday-night two-rakʿah prayer with repeated recitations and fifteen istighfārs dedicated to parents fulfills their right even after disobedience.", "reasons": "Bursevī cites reports from al-Iḥyāʾ and Qūt al-Qulūb for this distinct prescription."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q29", "question": "How grave is disobedience to parents?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q29/p1", "position": "It is among the worst major sins, paired with associating partners with God.", "reasons": "Al-Ḥasan reports a Prophetic scale in which good deeds culminate in giving one's life for God and sins culminate in parental disobedience. Study Quran cites the Prophet naming shirk and disrespect of parents among the greatest major sins."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q30", "question": "How does this injunction connect to other Qur'anic commands?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q30/p1", "position": "Kindness to parents is repeatedly paired with worship of God alone and follows the warning against shirk here.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān calls it a further call to obey God after Luqmān's warning. Ibn Kathīr compares 17:23; Study Quran compares 4:36, 29:8, 46:15 and 17:23 and says the parental command first appears in the covenant of 2:83. Al-Biqāʿī says gratitude to God entails gratitude to people. Al-Samīn notes the construction was discussed at 29:8."}, {"id": "31:14/q30/p2", "position": "The successive pregnancy hardship here complements 46:15's painful pregnancy and delivery; together they reinforce the parents' claim to kindness.", "reasons": "Samarrāʾī compares the two descriptions and says the paired ordeals strengthen the claim to iḥsān."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q31", "question": "How is the nūn of an before the imperative pronounced?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q31/p1", "position": "A reported form changes the nūn from kasra to ḍamma, anu, by phonetic assimilation before the imperative.", "reasons": "Qiraat-ER records and explains this pronunciation."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q32", "question": "How do a teacher's benefits compare with a parent's in gratitude?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q32/p1", "position": "A teacher can deserve greater gratitude because a parent gives mortal life while a teacher guides toward lasting or higher life.", "reasons": "Bursevī cites Alexander's comparison of father bringing him from heaven to earth and tutor lifting him toward heaven; Burzjumhr similarly contrasts mortal and lasting life."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q33", "question": "What does the human being's place in creation illustrate here?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q33/p1", "position": "The human being is creation's fruit and kernel, combining both worlds and receiving verbal revelation.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī reports al-Rāzī's tree image: the human is its fruit, kernel rather than rind, and completion."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q34", "question": "What larger point does gratitude to God make in the adjoining Luqmān passage?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q34/p1", "position": "Gratitude benefits and perfects the grateful human, while God is self-sufficient and already praised by creation.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr contrasts human benefactors' possible reciprocal gain with God's lack of need; turning away is human ingratitude. He cites 13:15 for creation's praise, says Luqmān's wisdom begins immediate gratitude on receiving a blessing, quotes 'praise is the head of gratitude,' and notes ḥamīd is used because God has no name from the gratitude root except al-Shakūr."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q35", "question": "Does the possessive yāʾ in lī have variant readings?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q35/p1", "position": "No reading disagreement is reported for it among the sūra's five possessive yāʾ forms.", "reasons": "Ibn Mujāhid counts five yāʾ al-iḍāfa forms in the sūra and says none has a variant reading."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q36", "question": "What teachings make up Luqmān's counsel in this passage?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q36/p1", "position": "It moves from rejecting shirk and honoring parents to awareness of God, prayer, right conduct, patience, and humble bearing and speech.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr surveys the connected counsel, naming each of these teachings."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q37", "question": "Why is Luqmān's counsel recounted to its audience?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q37/p1", "position": "It shows Arabs that their wise ancestors taught the Qur'an's guidance, exposes blind imitation of forefathers who followed Satan, and condemns punishing children for following Luqmān's teaching.", "reasons": "Iṣlāḥī explains the counsel's role in the sūra through this contrast with inherited conduct."}]}
{"id": "31:14/q38", "question": "Why use waṣṣaynā for the parental injunction?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:14/q38/p1", "position": "The intensive waṣṣā suits weighty religious and moral injunctions, while awṣā normally concerns material matters such as inheritance.", "reasons": "Samarrāʾī compares 2:132 and 4:131 with 4:11; he notes 19:31 as an exception, where awṣā concerns Jesus' prayer and alms while he is an infant and not legally responsible."}]}

{"id": "31:17/q01", "question": "How is the final yāʾ of yā bunayya read?", "turns_on": "Transmission and whether the final yāʾ preserves possessive inflection, opens after contraction or is lightened.", "positions": [{"id": "31:17/q01/p1", "position": "Doubled with kasra.", "reasons": "Jishumi relates kasra to the possessive form; Ibn Atiyya names Nafi, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Hamza, al-Kisai and Abu Bakr from Asim. Nashr gives Hafs in six occurrences, Abu Bakr at Hud and al-Bazzi at the last Luqman occurrence; Ibn Abi Barra gives Ibn Kathir fatha at the third."}, {"id": "31:17/q01/p3", "position": "Lightened with sukun.", "reasons": "Jishumi calls sukun original; Ibn Abi Barra reports it at the first occurrence, Qunbul at first and third, and Nashr gives Qunbul at the final Luqman occurrence. {"id": "31:17/q03", "question": "What does establishing prayer require?", "turns_on": "Outward observance or prayer's transforming effect on conduct.", "positions": [{"id": "31:17/q03/p1", "position": "Perform it fully with obligations, limits, conditions and appointed times.", "reasons": "Nahhas includes every right of the entrusted work; Tabari its bounds; Tabrisi and Ibn Kathir its time; Biqai its conditions; Ibn Ashur regularity. Islahi includes praying oneself and urging others."}, {"id": "31:17/q03/p2", "position": "Persist inwardly in avoiding indecency and wrongdoing.", "reasons": "Najm al-Din says abstention can be prayer without outward form, while outward form without restraint is not truly prayer."}]}
{"id": "31:17/q04", "question": "Why is prayer singled out?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:17/q04/p1", "position": "It perfects and purifies the worshipper after belief and is the chief worship directed to God.", "reasons": "Razi calls it sincere worship; Razi, Baydawi, Elmali, Bursevi and Alusi contrast perfecting self with helping others. Abu Hayyan calls it noblest turning to God. Biqai says it restrains wrongdoing and follows monotheism in rank. Bursevi says it reforms the soul more deeply than fasting and disciplines, which chiefly improve temperament; desire is especially hateful to God. Ibn Ashur calls it the pillar of deeds acknowledging God's authority; Tabatabai the pillar of religion; Islahi the foremost gratitude; Kuranyolu representative of worship."}]}
{"id": "31:17/q05", "question": "Was prayer taught in earlier communities?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:17/q05/p1", "position": "Yes; prayer and these acts were taught or required before, though prayer's form varied.", "reasons": "Razi notes different earlier forms; Nasafi and Abu Hayyan infer duties across nations; Islahi says all prophets and religions taught prayer; Biqai says no community may abandon this counsel."}]}
{"id": "31:17/q06", "question": "Why does prayer precede enjoining and forbidding?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:17/q06/p1", "position": "One perfects one's own worship, then helps perfect others.", "reasons": "Razi calls the latter prophetic work; Baydawi, Alusi, Elmali and Study Quran contrast self and others. {"id": "31:17/q07", "question": "Why is almsgiving omitted after prayer?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:17/q07/p1", "position": "It signals Luqman and his son's detachment from worldly provision.", "reasons": "Biqai makes prayer second only to monotheism and connects the omission with their asceticism."}]}
{"id": "31:17/q08", "question": "What good and wrong are meant?", "turns_on": "Whether the nouns specify faith and shirk, justice and injustice, or the full scope of good and wrong.", "positions": [{"id": "31:17/q08/p1", "position": "All divinely, rationally or legally approved good and condemned evil.", "reasons": "Tabari includes obedience and prohibitions; Tabrisi rational and legal vileness; Wahidi reports obedience and disobedience. Ibn Ashur includes one's own conduct."}, {"id": "31:17/q08/p2", "position": "Monotheism and worship are enjoined; shirk and idols are forbidden.", "reasons": "Abu al-Aliya, al-Suddi, Ibn Abbas, Muqatil and Ibn Jubayr are reported. Ibn Jawzi groups 9:71 and 9:112 with 31:17. Ibn Abbas calls shirk a wrong against oneself; Muqatil specifically says hidden or unrecognized shirk."}, {"id": "31:17/q08/p3", "position": "Justice is made manifest and injustice denounced.", "reasons": "Wahidi reports al-Kalbi's gloss."}]}
{"id": "31:17/q09", "question": "Must the adviser first practice what he teaches?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:17/q09/p1", "position": "Yes, one should correct and govern oneself before directing others.", "reasons": "Sulami reports beginning with oneself; Qushayri makes self-rule prerequisite. Qurtubi and Biqai cite poetry saying to restrain one's own wrong before claiming wisdom. Abu Hayyan says embody the advice; Ibn Ashur includes one's own conduct."}]}
{"id": "31:17/q10", "question": "What is the social purpose of enjoining and forbidding?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "31:17/q10/p1", "position": "They guide others and protect shared life by promoting good and restraining harm.", "reasons": "Razi associates them with prophets and learned successors. {"id": "33:72/q03", "question": "What is ٱلْأَمَانَةَ?", "turns_on": "General charge, particular trust, moral faculty, covenant, and inward perfection.", "positions": [{"id": "33:72/q03/p1", "position": "The general charge of obedience, religious duties, commands, prohibitions and accountability.", "reasons": "Ṭabarī prefers the unrestricted sense, including worldly trusts.
